abstractText: Background Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is the most prevalent congenital cardiac malformation and confers a markedly elevated risk of infective endocarditis (IE).Severe concurrent complications, including perivalvular abscess, ruptured aortic sinus aneurysm, pseudoaneurysm, and complete atrioventricular block(AVB), rarely coexist in a single patient, and afebrile atypical presentations further delay diagnosis. Cardiac computed tomography angiography (CTA) enables comprehensive preoperative anatomical mapping for complex BAV-IE, yet standardized imaging-driven management experience for this extreme disease spectrum remains scarce. Methods We report a 59-year-old afebrile male patient presenting with 4 months of exertional dyspnea. Preoperative cardiac CTA with 3D volume rendering was performed to delineate valvular, perivalvular, and aortic root lesions.A composite radical Bentall-based surgical procedure was delivered, with postoperative blood culture and 3-year serial echocardiographic follow-up. All imaging data were anonymized for publication. Results CTA confirmed congenital type 0 BAV, IE with perivalvular abscess, 18 mm coronary sinus rupture forming a 5.0×4.5 cm aortic root pseudoaneurysm, and third-degree atrioventricular block.Intraoperative debridement combined with aortic root replacement, multi-valvular repair, and temporary epicardial pacing was completed successfully.Streptococcus mitis was isolated from blood cultures.Over three years of follow-up, the mechanical valve remained functionally stable, graft flow stayed unobstructed, and all clinical symptoms completely resolved. Conclusions Cardiac CTA with 3D visualization provides definitive preoperative anatomical stratification for multi-complicated atypical BAV-IE.Early radical composite surgery guided by comprehensive imaging yields a favorable long-term prognosis, even in elderly afebrile patients with four concurrent severe cardiovascular complications.This case highlights the irreplaceable role of multimodal cardiac imaging in risk stratification and surgical planning for complex BAV-associated endocarditis.

title: Integrative SMR and multi-model machine learning characterize FCER1A- and INSIG1-associated phenotypes in arterial aging-related disease
authorString: Jiang S, Xiao D, Chen Y, Kuang Y, Chen X, Li Z, Zhang C, Li J.
abstractText: Background and aims : Global population aging has made age-related cardiovascular disease an urgent public health challenge, and inflammation is closely associated with arterial aging. This study aimed to identify inflammation-related molecular features associated with arterial aging-related disease using an integrative analytical framework. Methods : We integrated summary-data-based Mendelian randomization (SMR), machine learning, single-cell RNA sequencing, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. SMR used FinnGen coronary artery disease GWAS and GTEx v8 whole-blood eQTL data. Models were evaluated in GEO transcriptomic datasets; single-cell and macrophage-state analyses resolved cell-type expression patterns. Expression was assessed in serially passaged human umbilical vein endothelial cells and naturally aged C57BL/6J mice. Drug-response prediction, docking, and molecular dynamics simulations prioritized candidate compounds and assessed modeled interactions. Results : FCER1A and INSIG1 were preferentially expressed in macrophage populations and varied across connected macrophage states and inferred trajectories in diseased vessels. Their expression was also increased during serial-passage-associated endothelial senescence and in aged mouse arterial tissue. Computational analyses prioritized dihydrorotenone and entospletinib and supported plausible modeled interactions with the corresponding protein structures. Conclusions : The integrative analysis prioritized FCER1A and INSIG1 as molecular features associated with arterial aging-related disease and provided cell-type localization and experimental expression evidence. These results set the stage for follow-up mechanistic and pharmacological investigations to dissect causal relationships and explore their therapeutic relevance.

title: Profound Vasovagal Bradycardia and Hypotension During Lumbar Epidural Steroid Injection Leading to the Diagnosis of Previously Undetected Hypertensive Heart Disease: A Case Report
authorString: Ilo DI, Ilo IS, Chukwu IS, Okwara EC, Enegela EJ, Aneke Cs.
abstractText: Background: Epidural steroid injection (ESI) is a widely used interventional technique for the conservative management of chronic low back pain secondary to disc herniation. While generally safe, it carries a recognised, though uncommon, risk of vasovagal reactions, particularly in patients positioned sitting or in the setting of needle-related anxiety. Case presentation: We report the case of a 70-year-old retired woman, a known hypertensive, who had previously tolerated two lumbar ESIs uneventfully, each providing approximately eight months of effective analgesia. During a third ESI, performed in the sitting position with standard preloading and aseptic precautions, the patient became acutely hypotonic and unresponsive at the point of loss of resistance to air, with profound bradycardia (heart rate 34 beats/min), hypoxia (SpO2 88%), and hypotension (blood pressure 64/32 mmHg). The needle was withdrawn immediately, the patient repositioned supine, and resuscitated with supplemental oxygen, intravenous atropine, and ephedrine, with recovery within two minutes. Subsequent cardiology evaluation, including echocardiography and electrocardiography, revealed previously undiagnosed hypertensive heart disease with eccentric left ventricular hypertrophy, diastolic dysfunction, and mild pulmonary hypertension. She was cleared for the procedure after three weeks of optimisation and successfully completed the ESI uneventfully four weeks after the index event. Conclusion: This case highlights the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for profound vasovagal reactions during neuraxial procedures in elderly patients, even those with prior uneventful exposure, and underscores the value of thorough cardiovascular evaluation following such episodes, as they may unmask previously silent structural heart disease.

title: Neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio and late gadolinium enhancement in clinically suspected myocarditis: a multicentre retrospective study
authorString: Özkan MT, Güner A, Tanık VO, Kalkan S, Asil S, Kalkan K, Karaüzüm K, Levent F, Şahin T, Uygun İH, Uluöz S, Öncü M, Uslu E, Çomoğlu A, Gömleksiz BN, Çolak G, Ceylan MK, Akgün H, Ormancı D, Tunca Ç, Karpat MS, Yüksel UÇ, Güner EG, Tanık EB, Öztürk EK, Cansever AT, Alparslan B, Özlek B.
abstractText: Background Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging identifies myocardial involvement in myocarditis and carries prognostic weight. The neutrophil percentage-to-albumin ratio (NPAR) combines neutrophil predominance with serum albumin, a negative acute-phase reactant. Whether NPAR is associated with LGE, and whether it adds information to its individual components and to routinely available clinical data, is unknown. Methods This retrospective observational study included 1,055 adults with clinically suspected myocarditis who underwent CMR at seven tertiary cardiovascular centres in Türkiye between October 2022 and September 2025. All studies were reviewed centrally by three cardiovascular radiologists blinded to clinical and laboratory data (Fleiss' κ = 0.83). Variables significant on univariable analysis (p < 0.10) were entered into multivariable logistic regression models, the shape of the association was examined using restricted cubic splines, and the incremental value of NPAR over the clinical and laboratory model was assessed using discrimination and reclassification metrics. Results LGE was present in 285 patients (27.0%). NPAR was higher in the LGE-positive group [1.65 (1.40–1.92) vs. 1.29 (1.02–1.55); p < 0.001]. In the multivariable model, NPAR remained independently associated with LGE positivity (adjusted odds ratio per 1 standard deviation 4.381, 95% confidence interval 3.248–5.907; p < 0.001), and the Nagelkerke R² rose from 0.157 to 0.387. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a positive association across the observed range with evidence of non-linearity (p = 0.013). Adding NPAR increased the area under the curve of the model from 0.728 (0.687–0.768) to 0.839 (0.806–0.872) (difference 0.111; p < 0.001), with an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.194 (0.133–0.251) and a continuous net reclassification improvement of 0.843 (0.674–1.011), both p < 0.001. As a single marker, NPAR yielded an area under the curve of 0.750 (0.718–0.782) at a cut-off of 1.43, discriminating LGE better than either constituent (both p < 0.0001). Conclusions In clinically suspected myocarditis, NPAR was independently associated with CMR-defined LGE positivity, discriminated LGE better than either of its own components, and provided significant incremental discrimination and reclassification over a clinical and laboratory model. NPAR may serve as a low-cost adjunctive marker where access to CMR is constrained.

title: Associations of Empirically Derived Dietary Patterns with the Index of Cardiac Electrophysiological Balance in a Community-Dwelling Population: A Cross-Sectional Study
authorString: Yeerken M, Gu X, Dong J, Xu Y, Lu Y, Tang B.
abstractText: Background The index of cardiac electrophysiological balance (ICEB) and its heart rate-corrected form (ICEBc) reflect ventricular depolarization–repolarization balance. Their associations with habitual dietary patterns (DPs) remain unclear. Methods This community-based cross-sectional study included 1,840 adults from five study areas in Xinjiang, China. DPs were derived from a 16-item food-frequency questionnaire using principal component analysis with varimax rotation. ICEB and ICEBc were calculated as QT/QRS and Bazett-corrected QT/QRS, respectively. General linear models and restricted cubic splines evaluated quartile and nonlinear associations, with adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, lifestyle, anthropometric, and clinical covariates. Sensitivity analyses used the Fridericia-corrected index (ICEBcF).. Results Two DPs explained 43.95% of the variance in food-consumption frequency: “preserved vegetables and beverages” (DP1) and “fresh produce, red meat, and rice” (DP2). In the fully adjusted quartile analysis, DP1 was associated with ICEBc overall (P for overall = 0.020). Compared with the lowest quartile, ICEBc was higher in the second (β = 0.08; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.02–0.13), third (β = 0.09; 95% CI, 0.03–0.15), and fourth quartiles (β = 0.06; 95% CI, 0.01–0.12), without evidence of a linear trend (P for trend = 0.116). Splines suggested an inverted U-shaped association (P for overall = 0.017; P for nonlinearity = 0.008). Findings were similar for ICEBcF in quartile (P for overall = 0.009) and spline analyses (P for overall = 0.017; P for nonlinearity = 0.007). DP1 was not associated with ICEB, and DP2 was not associated with either primary outcome. Exploratory component analyses did not identify a clear driver of the DP1–ICEBc association. Conclusions Adherence to the “preserved vegetables and beverages” pattern was nonlinearly associated with ICEBc, with similar findings using Fridericia correction. These findings suggest a relationship between habitual diet and electrophysiological balance but do not establish causality or arrhythmic risk. Prospective studies are needed for confirmation.

title: Dissociating mechanical from biochemical platelet activation: dimethyl sulfoxide modulates the platelet membrane to attenuate shear-mediated activation
authorString: Sheikhlary S, Tran PL, Sweedo A, McKellar KR, Outridge CE, Valerio L, Yamaguchi JT, Sheriff J, Bluestein D, Italiano JE, Marty MT, Aspinwall CA, Redaelli A, Slepian MJ.
abstractText: Patients supported by implantable cardiovascular devices, including stents, prosthetic valves, and mechanical circulatory support systems, remain vulnerable to thromboembolic complications despite modern antithrombotic therapy. A central contributor is shear-mediated platelet activation, which differs in phenotype and pharmacologic sensitivity from activation induced by conventional biochemical agonists. Here we tested whether the platelet membrane can be perturbed to reduce shear-mediated activation, using dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) as a membrane-active probe. Gel-filtered platelets treated with DMSO were exposed to constant, dynamic ventricular-assist-device, and hyper-shear waveforms and assessed for thrombin generation, phosphatidylserine externalization, morphology, ultrastructure, and membrane probe anisotropy. DMSO at concentrations of 15% (v/v) or less reduced the measured shear-induced Platelet Activity State (PAS) across the tested shear regimes without overt membrane fragmentation under the tested conditions. Membrane anisotropy changed in a concentration-dependent, nonmonotonic pattern that coincided with the inhibitory concentration range. After shear exposure, DMSO-treated platelets retained a measurable arachidonic-acid-induced aggregatory response under the conditions tested. These findings provide functional evidence that shear-induced procoagulant activity can be attenuated while arachidonic-acid-induced activity remains detectable in the same platelet population, and they support membrane perturbation as a general strategy for studying, and potentially targeting, mechanically induced platelet responses, with membrane lipids such as cholesterol representing a plausible next class of fluidity-modulating agents.

title: Clinical Study on NAFLD Intervening in the Progression of Coronary Atherosclerosis by Affecting TREM2-Related Inflammatory Pathways Regulated by Adipose Tissue
authorString: Li W, Zhou H, Meng N, Liang X.
abstractText:
Objective : To investigate the effect of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) on the progression of coronary atherosclerotic heart disease (CCS) and its association with TREM2-related inflammatory pathways.

Methods:

A total of 56 CCS inpatients were divided into the NAFLD+CCS group (n=33) and CCS group (n=23) based on NAFLD diagnostic criteria. Basic clinical and biochemical indicators, liver/visceral fat content, and coronary atherosclerosis severity (GS score) were detected. Monocyte subsets (classical CD14++CD16-, intermediate CD14++CD16+, non-classical CD14+CD16++) were analyzed by flow cytometry. Serum sTREM2, IL-6, and IL-10 concentrations were measured by ELISA or enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Results Compared with the CCS group, the NAFLD+CCS group had significantly higher absolute monocyte count (MO), hs-CRP, GS score, and sTREM2 concentration (all P<0.05). Regarding monocyte subsets, the proportion of classical monocytes (CM) was lower (80.12%±4.38% vs. 83.93%±5.35%, P=0.005), while intermediate (IM: 4.83%±1.48% vs. 3.25%±1.53%, P=0.000) and non-classical monocytes (NCM: 8.53%±3.26% vs. 6.50%±3.17%, P=0.024) were higher in the NAFLD+CCS group. Levels of IL-6 and IL-10 were also significantly elevated in the NAFLD+CCS group (both P<0.001). Conclusion : NAFLD exacerbates systemic inflammation and coronary atherosclerosis in CCS patients, accompanied by abnormal monocyte subset distribution and increased sTREM2. It is speculated that TREM2 may regulate macrophage polarization via the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway, thereby mediating adipose tissue inflammation and participating in NAFLD-related atherosclerosis progression.

title: Effective arterial elastance as a predictor of fluid responsiveness in patients with septic shock：a prospective observational study
authorString: Tang J, Shen J, Cao Y, Shan L, Liu K.
abstractText: Background Assessment of fluid responsiveness is essential in the resuscitation of patients with septic shock. Effective arterial elastance (Ea) is a lumped index of arterial load; however, its ability to predict fluid responsiveness in these patients remains unknown. Methods This prospective observational study was conducted in the intensive care unit of Zhejiang Cancer Hospital. All enrolled patients underwent a 500mL fluid challenge (FC), and hemodynamic parameters, including cardiac output (CO) and mean arterial pressure (MAP), were recorded using the PiCCO system. Fluid responsiveness was defined as an increase in CO of > 10% after the fluid challenge, and arterial pressure responsiveness as an increase in MAP of > 10%. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was performed to evaluate the predictive ability of Ea. Correlations between Ea and FC-induced changes in CO and MAP were assessed. Results Forty-one patients were analysed, of whom 20 (49%) were fluid responders. Baseline Ea was significantly higher in fluid responders than in fluid nonresponders [2.43 (2.07–4.04) vs 1.82 (1.61–2.47) mmHg/mL, p = 0.022]. Baseline Ea predicted fluid responsiveness with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.710 (95% CI: 0.549–0.870, p = 0.022) and an optimal cut-off value of 2.00 mmHg/mL (sensitivity: 80%; specificity: 62%), but lacked predictive ability for arterial pressure responsiveness (AUC = 0.583, 95% CI: 0.361–0.781, p = 0.427). FC-induced percentage change in CO (ΔCO%) was moderately correlated with baseline Ea (ρ = 0.45, p = 0.004), whereas the percentage change in MAP (ΔMAP%) was not (ρ = −0.28, p = 0.080). Among the fluid responders, 15 (75%) were arterial pressure nonresponders. In this subgroup, Ea decreased significantly after the fluid challenge [1.91 (1.67–2.45) vs 2.43 (2.07–4.29) mmHg/mL, p = 0.001], and the percentage change in Ea (ΔEa%) was strongly correlated with both ΔCO% (ρ = −0.65, p = 0.002) and ΔMAP% (r = 0.67, p = 0.001). Conclusion In patients with septic shock, baseline Ea > 2.00 mmHg/mL predicts fluid responsiveness but not arterial pressure responsiveness. A significant decrease in Ea after a fluid challenge may explain the dissociation between fluid responsiveness and arterial pressure responsiveness.

title: Expanding the prenatal and postnatal phenotype spectrum of HEATR5B-related disorders
authorString: SCOTT H, Ha TT, Gardner A, Bennett MK, Anastasio N, Lazon J, Jacob M, Raum M, Pauly M, Wiesener A, Reis A, Badalato L, Hildebrandt F, Zion E, Jeffries L, Konstantino M, Ramond F, Juul TM, Larsen MB, Hansen L, Jackson M, Doyle H, Rice M, Chung C, Barnett C.
abstractText: Biallelic hypomorphic variants in HEATR5B were first reported in four individuals from two families with pontocerebellar hypoplasia, but no disease entity is listed for HEATR5B in OMIM, Mondo or similar databases; despite its ubiquitous expression across multiple organ systems, the gene-disease relationship remains limited to neurodevelopmental disorders. Genematching between 2021 and 2026, lead to the identification of 12 novel variants in HEATR5B , from 17 individuals in 11 unpublished families. Eight of these families showed autosomal recessive inheritance (seven homozygous, one compound heterozygous), while the remaining three carried de novo variants. Stillbirth and fetal hydrops were observed in 5/8 and 7/8 individuals respectively, and neurological phenotypes accounted for 10/14 of the postnatal cases; other organ systems, including genitourinary, cardiac, digestive and respiratory, were less frequently affected. This is the largest HEATR5B cohort to date, and highlights the perinatal lethality of HEATR5B -related disorders, and its multiorgan systemic involvement beyond neurodevelopmental disorders alone.

title: Dizziness and quality of life in Chagas disease patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices
authorString: Filgueiras PHC, Villar RTHOSG, Costa CAHDd, Souza AC, Eira BOd, Cirenza C, de Paola AAV.
abstractText: Purpose Residual symptoms, particularly dizziness, persist in many recipients of cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIED). We compared dizziness and quality of life in CIED patients with and without chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy (CCC). Methods Cross-sectional study of consecutive CIED outpatients. The primary outcome was the presence of dizziness on systematic clinical assessment; the Dizziness Handicap Inventory measured burden. Quality of life was assessed with the Short Form-36 Health Survey (SF-36). Analyses used Firth penalized logistic and multiple linear regression, plus mediation analysis. Results Of 100 patients (mean age 68.2 years, 59% women), 36 had CCC. The CCC group had lower ejection fraction (p = 0.039), worse functional class (p = 0.024), and more non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (50.0% vs 4.7%; p < 0.001). Dizziness was more frequent in CCC (83.3% vs 51.6%; p = 0.002) and remained independent after adjustment (odds ratio 3.96; 95% confidence interval 1.46–10.78; p = 0.007). Global SF-36 and its components were similar between groups, but dizziness was associated with lower global (45.6 vs 50.1; p = 0.026) and physical component (42.7 vs 50.0; p = 0.002) scores; mediation analysis showed a significant indirect effect of CCC on quality of life through dizziness. No drug class or comorbidity was associated with dizziness. Conclusion CIED recipients with CCC report dizziness more often than other etiologies, independently of structural and arrhythmic burden and of medication, and dizziness is associated with worse physical quality of life. The variables evaluated did not identify the mechanism, supporting systematic assessment of dizziness in follow-up.

title: Diagnostic Utility of Pentraxin-3 Compared With N-terminal-prohormone of B-Type Natriuretic Peptide (Nt-probnp) and Tumour Necrosis Factor-α (Tnf-α) in Dogs With Degenerative Mitral Valve Disease
authorString: Gunaratne U, Khor KH, Mustaffa-Kamal F, Kok MK, Noordin N, Tan EYM.
abstractText: Pentraxin-3 (PTX3) is a novel biomarker of interest in cardiovascular disease and injury. Despite this, there is limited literature on PTX3 as a veterinary biomarker. Another ubiquitous inflammatory marker, tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), has been studied extensively in dogs with DMVD, with mixed findings. The N-terminal-prohormone of B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is a routinely used biomarker of canine cardiac dysfunction. This study compared the diagnostic utility of PTX3 with TNF-α and NT-proBNP in dogs with DMVD. Serum NT-proBNP, PTX3, and TNF-α were measured in 50 client-owned dogs diagnosed and staged according to the ACVIM stages A-D. Echocardiographic variables, radiographic vertebral heart score (VHS) and vertebral left atrial size (VLAS), systolic blood pressure (SBP), and quality of life (QoL) scores were assessed. The Kruskal-Wallis test was used to compare PTX3, TNF-α, and NT-proBNP levels between different stages of DMVD, and the Jonckheere-Terpstra test assessed whether serum biomarker concentrations showed a significant ordered trend across progressively worsening DMVD across stages. Spearman’s correlation was used to assess the associations between biomarker levels, disease stage, QoL scores, SBP, radiographic, and echocardiographic parameters. Concentration of PTX3 and TNF-α did not differ significantly across DMVD stages, while only NT-proBNP showed significant variation between stages (p = 0.02). Jonckheere-Terpstra trend test revealed a significant ordered trend in serum NT-proBNP (p < 0.01), but not PTX3 and TNF-α across DMVD stages. NT-proBNP correlated significantly with DMVD stage, QoL score, VHS, VLAS, and echocardiographic variables including LVIDdn, LA:Ao (p < 0.01), and EF%, FS% (p = 0.02). NT-proBNP remains a reliable biomarker for diagnosis, disease monitoring, and prognosis assessment in canine DMVD. Future studies employing larger longitudinal cohorts will be essential to better elucidate the role of inflammatory markers in canine heart disease.

title: Evinacumab Enables Discontinuation of LDL Apheresis in Homozygous Familial Hypercholesterolemia: A Case Report
authorString: García Aguilar H, Fokine Dotsenko AGS, Vazquez-Del Campo AR, Gutiérrez–Múgica H, González M.
abstractText: Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH) is a rare genetic disorder characterized by markedly elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) levels and early cardiovascular disease. Despite intensive lipid-lowering therapy, achieving target LDL-C levels remains challenging, and many patients require lifelong LDL apheresis. We report a 33-year-old Mexican–Lebanese woman with confirmed HoFH and multiple comorbidities, including systemic lupus erythematosus. Severe hypercholesterolemia was evident from early childhood, with total cholesterol levels of approximately 800 mg/dL and development of xanthomas at age 3. The patient underwent long-term multimodal therapy, including statins, ezetimibe, PCSK9 inhibitors, and LDL apheresis initiated at age 9 and continued for approximately 20 years, achieving only partial lipid control. Evinacumab, an angiopoietin-like protein 3 (ANGPTL3) inhibitor, was initiated in adulthood as adjunctive therapy. Within two months, significant and sustained LDL-C reduction was achieved, allowing complete discontinuation of LDL apheresis. Follow-up demonstrated stable LDL-C levels between 180–225 mg/dL. This case highlights the clinical effectiveness of Evinacumab in patients with HoFH, demonstrating its potential to achieve sustained lipid reduction and eliminate the need for invasive apheresis. ANGPTL3 inhibition may represent a transformative strategy for improving long-term management and quality of life in this high-risk population, particularly in settings with limited access to apheresis.

title: Non-Invasive Photonic System for Disease Screening: Fingerprinting Exhaled-Breath Metabolites
authorString: Tatavarti R, Nadimpalli S, Kudipudi SNVG, Pardeshi T, Mahale P, Borhade O, Malolakannan S, Patel AM, Pachiyappan A.
abstractText: Compact, label-free optical transducers are attractive for real-time exhaled-breath screening. We report the characterization and classification performance of a low-power photonic elastic-backscatter sensing system (the Dr. T system) that interrogates injected gas mixtures with a 635 nm, <1 mW coherent diode-laser beam and records the back-scattered light on a two-dimensional silicon position-sensing detector (PSD) as a time series of intensity I and centroid coordinates (x, y) at 10 Hz. Seven calibration data sets were acquired in a sealed 0.11 L chamber—five disease-linked metabolite mixtures in a normal-air balance (CKD, SIBO, cystic fibrosis, COPD, heart disease), a healthy base-gas control, and an ambient control (19 records). Regression showed the beam-deflection axis (y vs x) to be a linear, reproducible common-mode signature of injection flow (slopes 0.18–0.24; R2 up to 0.98), whereas the optical response versus concentration (|I| vs C) is species-specific across a >20-fold slope range, constituting an optical fingerprint. A physically motivated feature space with Mahalanobis classification separated the four diseases carrying substantive metabolites at 100% leave-one-run-out recall; overall seven-class accuracy was 78.9%. Decisively, every substantive-metabolite disease was well separated from a base-gas control undergoing an identical chamber-pressure rise (D = 4.8–13.5), demonstrating that discrimination is driven by molecular optical signatures rather than common-mode pressure. The sensor can detect, discriminate, quantify and classify metabolite mixtures in vitro; signal-to-contrast enhancement for low-cross-section analytes, humidity compensation and radiometric calibration are identified as translation priorities.

title: One Toolchain, Six Domains: A Multiple-Case, Document-Based Study of Rapid IoT Prototypes Built in a One-Week Immersive Course on a Master’s Program in Applied Artificial Intelligence
authorString: Bento AC, Ortiz-Espinoza AA, Barceló-Alonso G, Silva JR, Falcón-Morales LE, Camacho-León S.
abstractText: This paper reports a document-based, multiple-case study of six Internet-of-Things (IoT) prototypes designed and simulated during a one-week immersive course, “IoT for Data Intelligence,” delivered in July 2026 within the professional Master in Applied Artificial Intelligence (Maestría en Inteligencia Artificial Aplicada, MNA) at Tecnológico de Monterrey. Six teams followed the same five-day toolchain IoT theory; Oracle Application Express (APEX), SQL, and REST service design; MIT App Inventor; ESP32/Wokwi simulation; and generative-AI integration and produced Wokwi-simulated prototypes spanning industrial energy monitoring, agricultural hazard response, residential automation, cardiovascular telemonitoring, industrial waste reduction, and precision agriculture. A fixed coding framework was applied across architecture, AI-integration pattern, platform-level failure modes, security debt, and Sustainable Development Goal alignment, distinguishing findings that the course structure itself prescribes from findings the teams introduced independently. The six cases converged on a shared five-layer architecture and, in a pattern only partly prescribed by the course, on keeping generative AI in an advisory or fail-safe-wrapped role. Deposited results were also compared, for illustrative purposes only, against the course’s internal competency rubric. An observed proposal from a Pontifical Catholic University of Chile’s collaboration is discussed as an informal reference point rather than as evidence for generalization. This paper discusses the implications and limits of this small, single-institution, single-cohort, simulation-only case set.

title: Extra-Large Blood Pressure Cuff Need and Cost Burden in United States Adults with Hypertension.
authorString: Sahoo S, Brady T, Grobman B, Juraschek SP, Cluett JL.
abstractText:
Background

Accurate home blood pressure (BP) monitoring depends on appropriate cuff sizing, but the prevalence and cost implications of extra-large cuff need among US adults with hypertension are unknown.

Methods

Using pooled data from 2017-2023 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) with survey weighting, we estimated the prevalence of having a mid-arm circumference >43cm among US adults with hypertension, overall and by race/ethnicity. We also categorized home BP monitors listed on the US Validated Device Listing as standard (accommodating arm circumferences from 22-43cm) or extra-large cuff compatible (accommodating arm circumferences >43cm).

Results

Approximately 6.6% of US adults with hypertension (∼ 7.2 million individuals) had an arm circumference >43cm. Prevalence was highest among Non-Hispanic (NH) Black adults (11.4%) followed by Other Race/Multiracial (8.2%), NH White (6.2%), Hispanic (5.3%) and NH Asian adults (0.9%). Of the 51 validated devices, only 22 (43.1%) accommodated arm circumferences >43cm. The mean total cost of an extra-large cuff compatible system was 32.7% higher ($99.06 versus $74.70 for standard devices).

Conclusions

More than 7 million US adults with hypertension require an extra-large BP cuff; the substantially higher cost of extra-large cuff-compatible devices represents an important and underrecognized barrier to accurate home BP monitoring.

title: Long-term health outcomes and comorbidities in cytochrome P450 oxidoreductase (POR) deficiency: a scoping review of evidence and knowledge gaps.
authorString: Kouri C, Thirukkumar A, Flück CE.
abstractText:
Lay summary

P450 oxidoreductase deficiency (PORD) is a rare genetic condition that affects many body systems because the POR enzyme supports dozens of important metabolic pathways. Most research has focused on early symptoms, such as hormone problems, differences in sex development, and bone abnormalities. Much less is known about how PORD affects people later in life. This review brings together current evidence and highlights possible long-term risks, including high blood pressure, liver and metabolic problems, reduced fertility, and bone health issues. Longer-term studies are urgently needed to understand these risks and to guide better care for individuals with PORD.

title: Sympathetic vascular transduction in adults with hypertension and obesity-associated hypertension.
authorString: Manferdelli G, Hissen SL, Wakeham DJ, Oghatiyan A, Davis SL, Sarma S, Levine BD, Fadel PJ, Hearon CM.

journal.medlineAbbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol
journal.title: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
journal.isoabbreviation: Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol

abstractText: Half of adult Americans have high resting blood pressure (BP). Although elevated muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA) is a common characteristic of essential hypertension, resting sympathetic activation is highly variable. This variability may relate to alterations in the transduction of MSNA to vasoconstriction. It is unknown if sympathetic vascular transduction is altered in hypertension, or how obesity, a common comorbidity, modifies vascular transduction. Sympathetic transduction was quantified in twelve normotensive (CON; age: 38±10 years, BMI: 25±3 kg/m<sup>2</sup>) and thirty hypertensive adults (12 non-obese [N-HTN]: age, 44±6 years, BMI: 27±3 kg/m<sup>2</sup>; and 18 with obesity [OB-HTN]: age: 40±10 years, BMI: 38±5 kg/m<sup>2</sup>). Continuous measurements of MSNA (microneurography), mean arterial pressure (MAP, photoplethysmography), and superficial femoral artery blood flow (LBF, doppler ultrasound) were used to calculate beat-by-beat leg vascular conductance (LVC; LBF/MAP). Transduction to LVC and MAP were quantified using signal averaging and compared using mixed-effects model with age, sex, race, and menopausal status as covariates. MSNA burst frequency (P=0.255) and incidence (P=0.417) were not different between groups. Sympathetic vascular transduction to multiple MSNA bursts was blunted in N-HTN (group: P=0.029), leading to a slower BP response compared to CON (interaction: P=0.030). The downregulation of sympathetic vascular transduction was less apparent in OB-HTN and associated with higher sympathetic transduction to diastolic BP compared to N-HTN (P=0.041). Compared to CON, sympathetic vascular transduction was attenuated in N-HTN but remained relatively preserved in OB-HTN. These data indicate that OB-HTN may be characterized by a greater contribution of sympathetic vascular transduction to blood pressure regulation.

title: Real-World Effectiveness of Biologic Therapy in Patients with Psoriasis: Metabolic Comorbidities and Treatment Outcomes.
authorString: Ghilencea AF, Costache DO, Căruntu C, Scheau C, Savulescu-Fiedler I, Dicu-Andreescu I, Cojocaru D, Costache RS.

journal.title: Romanian journal of internal medicine = Revue roumaine de medecine interne

abstractText:
Introduction

Psoriasis is a chronic systemic inflammatory disease, frequently associated with metabolic comorbidities that may influence therapeutic outcomes. Real-world evidence on the effectiveness of biologic therapy in this complex clinical context remains limited.

Objectives

To assess the prevalence of comorbidities in patients with psoriasis receiving biologic therapy and to identify factors associated with treatment response.

Methods

A retrospective observational study including 121 patients with chronic plaque psoriasis. Demographic data, comorbidities, biologic treatment class, and PASI/DLQI evolution at baseline and at standardized 6 and 12 months assessments was analyzed, together with the latest available clinical assessment recorded in 2025 after variable treatment durations.

Results

Comorbidities were present in 84.3% of patients, most frequently hepatic steatosis (73.6%), obesity (45.5%), hypertension (41.3%), and diabetes (19%). A significant improvement in PASI and DLQI scores was observed at all follow-up points (p < 0.001). Complete skin clearance (PASI 100) was achieved by 18.1% of the patients at 6 months and by 44.6% at 12 months. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, lower PASI scores at six months were independently associated with a higher likelihood of achieving PASI 100 at one year.

Conclusions

Biologic therapy was associated with marked clinical and quality-of-life improvement. Although metabolic comorbidities were highly prevalent, no significant association between metabolic comorbidities and PASI 100 response at one year was identified in the analyses performed.

title: Glycaemic Burden and Cognitive Screen-Positive Status in Younger Indian Adults with Long-Standing Type 2 Diabetes: A Cross-Sectional Study with a MoCA Cutoff Sensitivity Analysis in a Lower-Education Population
authorString: Lodha SM, Kumar S, Acharya S, Baweja R, Garg S.
abstractText:
ABSTRACT

Background

Structured cognitive screening in diabetes is recommended only from age 65, leaving younger adults with prolonged type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) exposure unmonitored. We quantified the association of HbA1c and diabetes duration with Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) screen-positive status in adults aged ≤ 60 years with T2DM of ≥ 5 years, and examined against matched controls how the MoCA cutoff (< 26, < 24, < 23) affects the group contrast in a lower-education population.

Methods

Cross-sectional study at a tertiary-care centre in North India: 110 adults with T2DM and 50 controls frequency-matched for age, sex, and education. Within diabetics, HbA1c and duration were modelled continuously by modified Poisson regression at each pre-specified cutoff and by Spearman correlation with MoCA total score. Prevalence ratios (PR) for diabetics versus controls at each cutoff were adjusted for age, sex, education, BMI, and hypertension.

Results

Within diabetics, MoCA total score correlated with HbA1c (ρ = −0.456) and duration (ρ = −0.318; both p < 0.001). Screen-positive prevalence rose 5% per 1% HbA1c at < 26 (PR 1.05, 95% CI 1.02-1.09), 12% at < 24 (PR 1.12, 1.06-1.18), and 17% at < 23 (PR 1.17, 1.09-1.26), and 11% per year of duration at < 23 (PR 1.11, 1.06-1.17). Median education was 10 and 9 years; 76.0% of controls screened positive at < 26, and the diabetes association was cutoff-dependent: adjusted PR 1.08 (0.89-1.29) at < 26, 1.70 (1.10-2.63) at < 24, and 6.72 (2.23-20.23) at < 23, where 44.5% of diabetics versus 6.0% of controls screened positive (absolute difference 38.5 percentage points, 95% CI 25.0 to 48.7).

Conclusions

In working-age adults with long-standing T2DM, screen-positive prevalence rose continuously with HbA1c at every cutoff, a glycaemic signal independent of threshold choice. The standard < 26 cutoff flagged over three-quarters of both groups and could not triage; < 23 separated diabetics from controls. Screen-positive status is not a diagnosis; MoCA triage at a population-appropriate cutoff in this group warrants prospective validation against a neuropsychological reference standard.

title: Self Reported Metabolic Disease Across the Adult Life Course in Palestine: Associations With Dietary Preferences, Lifestyle Behaviors, and Depressive Symptoms in an Online Cross Sectional Survey
authorString: Motan D, Lahlouh MM, Omari L, Mohammed SA, Ghanam ZA, Maqboul LS, Mhameed HM, Tbeileh MA, Morad L, Alkaraja J, Taha B, Massarwa F.
abstractText: Background Metabolic conditions are increasing in low resource settings, yet evidence linking age, dietary behaviors, lifestyle factors, and depressive symptoms in Palestine is limited. This cross sectional study aimed to evaluate dietary behaviors, lifestyle risk factors, and self reported metabolic diseases in Palestine. Methods An online questionnaire recruited Palestinian residents aged 18 years or older through nonprobability snowball sampling from 9 to 17 June 2026. Metabolic conditions included hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, or insulin resistance. Depressive symptoms were assessed using the CES D 10. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated independent correlates. Results Among 847 participants, age was 33.58 years; 85.0% were female, and 80.6% were university educated. The prevalence of any metabolic disease was 16.1%. Hypertension, diabetes, insulin resistance, and dyslipidemia were reported by 6.5%, 5.5%, 5.4%, and 3.3%, respectively. Among 703 with valid CES D 10 totals, 62.4% screened positive. Prevalence rose from 5.9% at ages 18 to 24 to 46.2% at 55 years or older. Each ten year age increase was associated with higher odds (AOR 2.16; 95% CI 1.81 to 2.57). Preference for hot or spicy foods was also independently associated (AOR 2.14; 95% CI 1.30 to 3.52). Conclusions Advancing age was the dominant correlate of self reported metabolic disease. The spicy food association is hypothesis generating because preference rather than intake was measured. Earlier risk assessment, grounded nutrition education, and mental health support should be evaluated in resource constrained Palestinian settings.

title: Dietary Index for Gut Microbiota and Prevalent Hypertension in Chinese Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study of Metabolic, Inflammatory, and Microbiota-Related Pathways
authorString: Xue Y, Lin J.
abstractText: Background The Dietary Index for Gut Microbiota (DI-GM) is a literature-based dietary index designed to characterize dietary patterns potentially supportive of a favorable gut microbiota. Evidence regarding the association between DI‑GM and hypertension in Chinese populations is scarce. We investigated the association between DI-GM and hypertension and explored potential metabolic, inflammatory, and gut microbiota-related pathways. Methods This community-based cross-sectional study included 1,700 Chinese adults aged ≥ 20 years. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated 112-item semi-quantitative food frequency questionnaire, and DI-GM scores were calculated based on 14 food components. Hypertension was defined by blood pressure measurements, physician diagnosis, or antihypertensive medication use. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations between DI-GM and hypertension with sequential adjustment for demographic, lifestyle, dietary, anthropometric, cardiometabolic, inflammatory, renal, and gut microbiota-related factors. Mediation analyses explored potential indirect associations through HOMA-IR, hs-CRP, NLR, TMAO, and LPS, recognizing the cross-sectional nature of these analyses. Results Higher DI-GM scores were associated with lower BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, hs-CRP, TMAO, and LPS, and with higher HDL-C and eGFR. In crude analysis, each one-unit increase in DI-GM was associated with lower odds of prevalent hypertension (OR = 0.933, 95% CI: 0.889–0.979), and participants in Q4 had lower odds than those in Q1 (OR = 0.714, 95% CI: 0.539–0.945). After adjustment for dietary and anthropometric factors, the association was markedly attenuated and became non-significant (fully adjusted Q4 vs. Q1 OR = 1.142, 95% CI: 0.802–1.626). Exploratory mediation analyses suggested potential indirect associations through HOMA-IR (25.8%), hs-CRP (21.1%), and TMAO (12.8%), although these should not be interpreted as causal due to the cross-sectional design. Conclusions Higher DI-GM was associated with a favorable cardiometabolic profile and lower levels of several gut microbiota-related biomarkers, but its association with hypertension was not independent of broader dietary and cardiometabolic characteristics. Exploratory mediation analyses identified statistical indirect associations involving HOMA-IR, hs-CRP, and TMAO; these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of causal mediation given the cross-sectional study design.

title: Meat Preference–Intake Discordance and Incident Cardiometabolic Disease in UK Biobank: A Prospective Cohort Study
authorString: Zhu Q, Tan Y, Yang Y, Shi X, Cai S, Zheng L, Song Z, Zhao A.
abstractText: Background Dietary intake and food preference are examined separately in nutritional epidemiology. Whether meat preference-intake discordance is associated with cardiometabolic disease (CMD) risk remains unclear. Methods We included 168,163 UK Biobank participants without prevalent CMD. Meat preference was assessed using the Food Preference Questionnaire, and habitual intake from repeated food-frequency assessments. Standardised preference minus standardised intake defined preference-intake discordance. Cox models, stratified analyses, generalised random forests, and counterfactual mediation analyses assessed incident CMD, heterogeneity, and pathways. Results During follow-up, 39,428 incident CMD cases occurred. Overall meat preference > intake was not significantly associated with CMD after full adjustment (HR 1.027, 95% CI 0.994–1.061). Preference > intake for beef, lamb, and pork was associated with higher CMD risk (HRs 1.045, 1.041, and 1.052), especially for hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Overall discordance was associated with CMD among low meat consumers (HR 1.078, 95% CI 1.022–1.136). HbA1c was a consistent positive mediator; liver- and bilirubin-related markers showed negative indirect effects suggestive of statistical suppression. Conclusions Meat preference-intake discordance was not uniformly associated with CMD risk; relevance varied by meat subtype and intake context. Preference-aware dietary assessment may refine individualised CMD risk evaluation.

title: Clinicopathological Features and Prognosis of Acute Interstitial Nephritis: A Study of 26 Patients
authorString: Nie G, Wei J, Li H, Wang D, Wang X.
abstractText: Objective : Acute interstitial nephritis (AIN) is an acute kidney injury (AKI) characterized by renal interstitial inflammation and tubular damage. This study aims to clarify its clinical features, etiologies, and prognosis. Methods: Clinical data from 26 AIN patients were retrospectively analyzed, including demographics, manifestations, lab tests, ultrasound, pathology, etiology, and outcomes. Results: Mean age was 54.8 years, with 53.8% aged 51–70 years. Females accounted for 61.5% (M:F=1:1.6). Hypertension (42.3%) and diabetes (19.2%) were common comorbidities. Digestive symptoms (38.5%) were the most frequent presentation. AKI occurred in 88.5%, all stage 3, and 38.5% received short-term hemodialysis. Lab findings showed elevated creatinine, BUN, and uric acid, with mild anemia in some. Renal ultrasound revealed increased cortical echogenicity (42.3%) and cysts (23.0%). Biopsy demonstrated interstitial inflammatory infiltration (mainly lymphocytes) in all cases, and 76.9% had interstitial fibrosis. Drug-related causes accounted for 30.8%, while 30.8% remained unknown. Eighteen patients received glucocorticoids. After 3 months, 22 patients were followed up, with a renal recovery rate of 95.5%. Conclusion: AIN is more common in middle-aged and elderly women, with drugs being a major causative factor. It typically presents as severe AKI. Renal biopsy reveals characteristic interstitial inflammation. With active treatment, the overall prognosis is favorable. Emphasis should be placed on preventing and early identifying drug-induced kidney injury.

title: Ophthalmological findings in children with metopic craniosynostosis
authorString: Constant A, Touze R, Paternoster G, Arnaud E, Khonsari R, Bremond-Gignac D, Robert M.
abstractText:
Introduction: Trigonocephaly is a form of craniosynostosis resulting from premature fusion of the metopic suture. It is the second most common of single-suture craniosynostoses, yet ophthalmological manifestations associated with this condition remain under-reported. This study aimed to characterize ophthalmological outcomes of children with trigonocephaly and determine whether targeted visual screening is warranted.

Methods:

We conducted a retrospective review of children with trigonocephaly managed in our institution between 2020 and 2024 who underwent a complete ophthalmological evaluation, including visual acuity testing, refraction, and oculomotor assessment.

Results:

Twenty-eight children met the inclusion criteria. Median age at evaluation was 5.2 years (range: 0.3–11.7) with a male predominance (68%). The mean best corrected visual acuity was 0.07 ± 0.12 LogMAR, including five (18%) children with a history of amblyopia. Strabismus was documented in seven patients (25%), most commonly exotropia (57%). The mean refractive spherical equivalent was + 1,55 ± 1.65 diopters (D). Seventeen eyes (30%) demonstrated clinically significant astigmatism (> 1 D), with a mean cylindrical value of 0,91 ± 0,85 D. The astigmatism axis was with-the-rule in 71%, oblique in 26% and against-the rule in 3% of eyes. One child (3.3%) exhibited papilledema suggestive of intracranial hypertension. Two children (three eyes) presented congenital cataract.

Conclusion:

Children with trigonocephaly exhibit a high prevalence of visual abnormalities, including refractive errors, strabismus, and in a very rare situations, signs of intracranial hypertension. These findings support the need of systematic, early, and longitudinal ophthalmological surveillance to facilitate prompt diagnosis and management of potential visual outcomes.

title: Presenting Symptom Type and Use of Catheter Ablation in Patients with Newly Diagnosed Atrial Fibrillation
authorString: Niimi N, Kohsaka S, Ikemura N, Ueda I, Nakamaru R, Kimura T, Katsumata Y, Nishiyama T, Tanimoto K, Takatsuki S, Ieda M.
abstractText: Background Atrial fibrillation (AF) frequently presents with a broad spectrum of symptoms, including non-specific complaints such as dyspnea, fatigue, dizziness, or syncope that may influence treatment decision. We examined, in patients with newly diagnosed AF, whether symptom type was associated with selection of catheter (CA) ablation and subsequent 1-year AF-specific health status. Methods We analyzed 2,848 newly diagnosed AF patients in the multicenter AF outpatient registry in 2012–2018. Presenting symptoms were categorized as palpitations, or non-palpatory symptoms (dizziness/syncope, dyspnea, or fatigue). AF-specific health status was measured at baseline and 1 year using the Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life overall summary score (AFEQT-OS). Symptom-control strategies were classified as rate control, antiarrhythmic drug therapy, or CA. Multivariate models were used to evaluate factors associated with CA selection and to estimate adjusted 1-year AFEQT-OS scores according to treatment strategy and presenting symptom type. Results Mean age was 68 ± 11 years and baseline AFEQT-OS score was 77.0 ± 17.7. Non-palpatory symptoms were common, including dyspnea in 43.9%, fatigue in 37.3%, and dizziness or syncope in 33.6%. During follow-up, 38.1% of patients underwent CA. Palpitations were independently associated with selection of CA (adjusted odds ratio 1.29; 95% confidence interval, 1.03–1.61, whereas non-palpatory symptoms were not. At 1 year, CA was associated with better AF-specific health status than rate control across symptomatic subgroups, with adjusted marginal mean differences in AFEQT-OS ranging from 7.3–8.1 points. There was no evidence that the association between CA and 1-year AFEQT-OS differed according to presenting symptom type. Conclusions Palpitations may preferentially drive CA selection in newly diagnosed AF, although the association between CA and better 1-year health status was similar magnitude across the evaluated symptom profiles

title: Multimodal 3D imaging reveals a central role for lysosomes in dissolution of cholesterol crystals by macrophages
authorString: Akkerman V, Juhl AD, Egebjerg JM, Pratsch C, Werner S, Schneider G, Willms T, Müller P, Kapishnikov S, Wüstner D.
abstractText:
Formation of cholesterol crystals (CCs) is a key event during the development of atherosclerosis, but the molecular mechanisms of their degradation within cells are poorly understood. By incorporating the fluorescent cholesterol analogue TopFluor-Cholesterol (TF-Chol) into CCs, we were able to visualize the uptake of CCs in macrophages using correlative fluorescence and soft X-ray microscopy. Using quantitative 3D live-cell imaging, we show that CCs are processed in late endosomes and lysosomes (LE/Lys), resulting in formation of TF-Chol containing lipid droplets (LDs) over time. Inhibition of lysosomal sterol export with U18666A caused accumulation of TF-Chol in LE/Lys, and inhibition of lysosomal acidification with bafilomycin A1 led to reduced dissolution of the CCs. Using a novel assay combined with 3D image processing, we show that large CCs in contact with macrophages are processed via lysosomal exocytosis followed by extracellular and intracellular degradation of CCs. Treating macrophages with a fluorescent version of cyclodextrin (CD) promoted the dissolution of CCs and enhanced the formation of LDs enriched with TF-Chol. The majority of fluorescent CD co-localized with a marker for LE/Lys during this process, suggesting that intracellular delivery to LE/Lys may contribute to the dissolution of CCs. Dehydroergosterol (DHE) is an intrinsically fluorescent sterol closely mimicking the properties and behavior of cholesterol. DHE is known to self-associate into aggregates and crystals, and by using fluorescence spectroscopy and specialized ultraviolet (UV) microscopy, we found that CD enhances the dissolution of DHE crystals in vitro and in cells. Together, our findings highlight the lysosomal pathway as responsible for dissolution of CCs, cholesterol trafficking, and efflux in macrophages.

title: RNA Splicing of the REST Gene by SRRM4 in Vascular Smooth Muscle Cells Promotes Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Development
authorString: Li Y, Wang Y, Ni Q, Yang S, Qi H, Yao Y, Wang H, Xu W, Yuan K, Lv L, Guo X, Ye M, Xue G, Tang WH, Pu J, Zhang L.
abstractText:
ABSTRACT

Background

The progression of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is closely associated with the phenotypic switch of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMC). While members of the Serine/Arginine-rich splicing factor (SRs) superfamily are increasingly acknowledged for their pivotal role in modulating cell phenotype, the specific contribution of these factors to AAA development has remained underexplored.

Methods

Through integrated analyses the whole transcriptome of human and murine AAA tissues derived from clinical samples and animal models, we identified serine-arginine repeat matrix 4 (SRRM4) as a candidate gene regulating AAA formation. To investigate the role of SRRM4 in AAA formation, we used global and VSMC-specific SRRM4-knockout mice to construct AAA mouse models in two different ways. The impact of SRRM4 on AAA was further investigated in in vivo and in vitro models

Results

Elevated levels of SRRM4 mRNA and protein were observed in VSMC from both human and murine AAA tissues. Targeted silencing of SRRM4 in VSMC (but not in endothelial or myeloid cells) significantly attenuated AAA formation in both AngII- and CaCl 2- induced mouse models. Our results identify the RE1 silencing transcription factor (REST) as a critical target gene of SRRM4 in AAA, a master regulator of cellular phenotypic stability. We show that SRRM4 modulates VSMC phenotype through alternative splicing of the REST gene, resulting in a non-functional REST4 isoform. Furthermore, our study shows that REST directly represses STAT1, a mechanism by which SRRM4 influences VSMC phenotypic transition. Regarding clinical significance, inhibition of both STAT1 expression and function was shown to be beneficial in preventing AAA formation and slowing disease progression in mouse models.

Conclusions

This investigation uncovers a previously unrecognized role of SRRM4-mediated splicing of the REST gene in the progression of AAA and identifies a novel REST/STAT1 axis critical in the phenotypic modulation of VSMC. The findings of this study may provide insights for the development of innovative therapeutic strategies for AAA.

What is New?

Our study demonstrates that the RNA splicing factor SRRM4 (serine/arginine repetitive matrix 4) expression is increased in human and murine abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) tissues and unveils a previously undescribed role of SRRM4 in regulating AAA development. SRRM4 promotes AAA development and progression through inducing splicing of REST (RE1 silencing transcription factor) gene and upregulating STAT1 (signal transducer and activator of transcription 1) expression, which result in extracellular matrix degradation, inflammation, and VSMC phenotypic switching. Our study provides proof-of-concept evidence indicating the therapeutic value of STAT1 inhibition in AAA prevention and treatment.

What Are the Clinical Implications?

Our study defining a novel mechanism underlying the SRRM4/REST/STAT1 axis is crucial for developing new therapeutic strategies for AAA. Based on these findings, we have initiated a prospective study (REST4-AAA; ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07056491 ) to evaluate REST4 expression levels in serum of AAA patients and explore its potential as a serum biomarker for AAA prediction Our findings indicate that fludarabine, a clinically available agent reported to selectively suppress STAT1, effectively attenuates AAA progression in mice, suggesting its potential for repurposing as a therapeutic strategy for AAA.

title: AGA Clinical Practice Update on the Evaluation and Management of Metabolic Dysfunction- and Alcohol-Associated Liver Disease: Expert Review.
authorString: Arab JP, Malhi H, Winder GS, Fontana RJ.

journal.title: Clinical gastroenterology and hepatology : the official clinical practice journal of the American Gastroenterological Association

abstractText:
Description

Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is the leading cause of chronic liver disease and liver-related mortality in the United States. The 2023 multisociety consensus nomenclature was intended to develop a more evidence-based framework regarding the differing forms of SLD, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), metabolic dysfunction- and alcohol-associated liver disease (MetALD), and alcohol-associated liver disease. The purpose of this American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) Clinical Practice Update expert review is to provide Best Practice Advice regarding the diagnosis, staging, and treatment of MetALD.

Methods

This expert review was commissioned and approved by the AGA Institute Clinical Practice Updates Committee and the AGA Governing Board to provide timely guidance on a topic of high clinical importance to the AGA membership. The document underwent internal peer review by the Clinical Practice Updates Committee and external peer review through the standard procedures of Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology. These BPA statements were drawn from a review of the published literature and from expert opinion. Because systematic reviews were not performed, these BPA statements do not carry formal ratings regarding the quality of evidence or strength of the presented considerations. BEST PRACTICE ADVICE STATEMENTS BEST PRACTICE ADVICE 1: Patients with SLD can be classified into MASLD, MetALD, and alcohol-associated liver disease categories by the presence of cardiometabolic risk factors and the quantity of alcohol consumed in grams per week (ideally over ≥3 months), using the thresholds of ≈140 to 350 g/wk in women and 210 to 420 g/wk in men for MetALD. BEST PRACTICE ADVICE 2: All patients with steatotic liver disease, including MetALD, should be assessed initially and at least annually thereafter for alcohol use via patient interview, completion of validated alcohol use questionnaires, and/or measurement of serum and/or urine alcohol biomarkers. BEST PRACTICE ADVICE 3: Alcohol consumption increases the extent of hepatic steatosis accumulation and fibrosis progression in a dose-dependent manner in nearly all forms of chronic liver disease, including those with MetALD. Therefore, all patients should be advised to discontinue alcohol use, recognizing that abstinence may be preceded by periods of use reduction and intermittent use. BEST PRACTICE ADVICE 4: A tiered, noninvasive strategy that combines routine blood-based biomarkers with simple fibrosis scores, such as the Fibrosis-4 Index, should be used to identify low-risk patients with MetALD and to triage those at indeterminate or high risk to second-line tests (eg, elastography or serum Enhanced Liver Fibrosis test) for detection of advanced fibrosis and cirrhosis. BEST PRACTICE ADVICE 5: Vibration-controlled transient elastography and magnetic resonance-based techniques are noninvasive tools that objectively assess the fibrosis stage and steatosis burden in patients with MetALD; however, liver stiffness values should be interpreted cautiously in the presence of active alcohol use, which can transiently increase stiffness. BEST PRACTICE ADVICE 6: Medical management of MetALD should include dietary counseling and replenishment of micronutrient deficiencies (folate, thiamine, vitamin D) as well as aerobic exercise to improve body weight and muscle mass, along with treatment of concomitant cardiometabolic risk factors. BEST PRACTICE ADVICE 7: The safety and efficacy of United States Food and Drug Administration-approved treatments for noncirrhotic MASLD (ie, resmetiron and semaglutide) has not been formally studied in MetALD. However, preliminary data suggests that glucagon-like peptide-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonists may reduce alcohol cravings and consumption and improve hepatic parameters. BEST PRACTICE ADVICE 8: Medical management of patients with MetALD and moderate or severe alcohol use disorder should include use of alcohol use disorder pharmacotherapy and behavioral approaches to reduce alcohol consumption. BEST PRACTICE ADVICE 9: Endobariatric and bariatric surgery are not advisable for patients with MetALD due to the lack of safety and efficacy data as well as concerns regarding accelerated liver disease progression with continued alcohol use after surgery.

title: Snare-Free Endoscopic Tricuspid Valve Repair Using Percutaneous Venous Smart Cannulation: A Descriptive Cohort Study
authorString: Balan R, Massoudy P, Harpa MM, Brînzaniuc K, Schwarz J.
abstractText:
Background:

Minimally invasive and endoscopic techniques have expanded the surgical options for tricuspid valve repair. Conventional approaches often require manual snaring of the venae cavae, which can increase procedural complexity and invasiveness, especially in redo or advanced heart failure settings. This study describes a snare-free totally endoscopic approach to tricuspid valve repair utilizing percutaneous venous selfexpanding cannulation.

Methods:

Between 2020 and 2025, 32 consecutive patients with severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) underwent totally endoscopic tricuspid valve repair using a standardized snare-free technique. Venous drainage was achieved via percutaneous femoral cannulation with a self-expanding venous cannula, providing optimal central venous decompression without external tourniquets or loops. All clinical, intraoperative, and early postoperative parameters were systematically collected and analyzed using descriptive statistical methodology.

Results:

Endoscopic tricuspid valve repair was successfully completed in all 32 patients. The mean total cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) time was 145.9 ± 35.8 minutes, and the mean aortic cross-clamp duration was 92.4 ± 24.5 minutes. The early postoperative safety profile was characterized by an all-cause 30-day mortality rate of 3.1% (n = 1) and zero cases of clinically relevant hemolysis (0.0%)The mean intensive care unit stay was 6.0 ± 4.9 days, and the mean total hospital length of stay was 15.4 ± 9.7 days.

Conclusion:

Snare-free totally endoscopic tricuspid valve repair using a percutaneous self-expanding venous cannulation is a safe, technically feasible, and reproducible technique. This structural approach simplifies right atrial endoscopic visualization, eliminates the complications associated with deep caval-dissection, and demonstrates highly stable early clinical and electrophysiological outcomes.

title: Automated Detection of Coronary Artery Calcification via Machine Learning Analysis of 12-Lead Electrocardiograms
authorString: Yalcin M, Iyigun U, Pinarbasili T, Durak A, Kahramanogullari F, Gurses C, Cagirci G.
abstractText:
Background:

Coronary artery calcification (CAC) is a critical marker of subclinical atherosclerosis, yet its primary diagnostic tool, coronary computed tomography (CT), is limited by cost and radiation. We aimed to develop and validate a robust machine learning framework to identify significant CAC (Agatston score ≥100) using features extracted from routine 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs), including legacy archives stored as PDFs.

Methods:

This retrospective study utilized 382 consecutive patient records. A novel signal-processing pipeline was developed to convert PDF-based ECGs into standardized 500-Hz digital waveforms (WFDB format). From these signals, 360 morphological and temporal features were extracted using the NeuroKit2 library. To ensure clinical reliability and prevent optimistic bias, a Balanced Random Forest (BRF) classifier was integrated into a repeated “inner-outer” nested cross-validation framework combined with Minimum Redundancy Maximum Relevance (mRMR) feature selection.

Results:

The mRMR-BRF model demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy with a grand mean AUC of 0.8211 (95% CI: 0.8018–0.8404), outperforming standard algorithms. Explainability analysis via SHAP identified age, ST-segment level in lead V4, T/QRS ratio in lead III, and QRS duration dispersion as the most significant predictors. These features suggest that latent electrical signatures of subclinical myocardial remodeling and impaired perfusion are detectable via AI-enhanced ECG analysis.

Conclusion:

Our framework establishes digitized 12-lead ECGs as a scalable and non-invasive digital biomarker for significant CAC. By enabling the quantitative analysis of legacy PDF archives and providing high predictive stability through nested validation, this approach offers a cost-effective pre-screening tool to prioritize high-risk patients for definitive imaging and early preventive intervention.
